study.method: deterministic synthetic AST generation plus a separate Python full-text reference interpreter
study.case_generation_seed_formula: accepted: 10000 + family_index*1000 + variant*17 + 1; mutations: 90000 + mutation_index*1000 + variant*19 + 3
study.token_accounting_model: one UTF-8 byte equals one abstract input-use token; compiler invoked with --chars-per-token 1
study.complete_request: decoded template placeholders are substituted with full UTF-8 argument text before byte usage is counted
study.oracle: Omega(M,k,Q): SHA-256 of the fixed seed, canonical resolved contract M, per-contract ordinal k, and complete rendered request Q chooses a full ASCII response of 0..max_tokens bytes
study.retry_oracle: retry success/failure is a deterministic shared schedule keyed by seed, retry ordinal, and attempt index
scope_limitations: synthetic generated workflows; not exhaustive over the language
no provider adapter, real tokenizer, provider request envelope, invoice, timing, or output-text claim
only no-declassification generated cases are included
finite no-witness rejection probes are unknown, not labeled false positives
the generated byte-token assumption is controlled and does not imply provider billing soundness

failure_criteria: exit nonzero if any generated accepted case is rejected by orchc check
exit nonzero if any accepted case has differing reference request or usage traces across secret assignments
exit nonzero if a generated request exceeds its byte-accounting premise, a response exceeds its cap, or an execution exceeds budget
exit nonzero if any expected mutation is accepted or lacks the relational E236 diagnostic
do not fail solely because a rejected case has no distinguishing witness in the finite probe grid
